featured.title: Ramayana Nears ₹1,700 Crore Worldwide, Passes Dhurandhar 2 in the US
featured.excerpt: Day 18 added ₹35.60 crore net in India as the worldwide gross hit ₹1,693.50 crore — and its $28.4 million US total is now the highest ever for an Indian film.
featured.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita in Ramayana. The film reached Rs 1,693.50 crore worldwide gross in 18 days and set a new all-time US record for an Indian film at $28.4 million.
featured.nri_angle: The film's $28.4 million US total is a new all-time benchmark for an Indian film in America, with overseas markets supplying a third of its global gross.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith Defends Overseas Data Centres After Trump's Penalty Threat
just_in.excerpt: On Face the Nation, Smith split AI training sites from the cloud facilities that must sit near customers — while the Treasury secretary said he had not discussed Trump's proposal with him.
just_in.image_caption: Microsoft President Brad Smith in a portrait photograph. Smith told CBS Face the Nation that cloud data centres serving overseas customers must be located near those customers, after President Trump threatened penalties on companies building data centres abroad.
just_in.nri_angle: Microsoft's $17.5 billion India build-out in Chennai, Hyderabad and Pune sits inside the policy debate, but neither side named India as a target and no change was announced.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: A. R. Rahman Spent Three Years on 'Ramayana' Music, Turned Down 10–12 Films
just_in.excerpt: At IFFI in Panaji, the composer said he set aside almost everything else for Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic, co-composing with Hans Zimmer — some pieces went through 12–13 versions.
just_in.image_caption: A. R. Rahman with the Banaras team at a press conference during the International Film Festival of India in Goa.
just_in.nri_angle: Rahman and Hans Zimmer's three-year score is the musical backbone of the Diwali epic diaspora audiences are watching in theatres now.

just_in.excerpt: The former federal industry minister from Mississauga beat MPP Lee Fairclough by less than a point after a nine-month race, and now has to rebuild a party that holds 14 seats.

just_in.title: Deaf Graduate's AI Alarm SIVO.GO Wins UK James Dyson Award and £5,000
just_in.excerpt: Gargi Agrawalla, 23, built SIVO.GO from her own experience of missing alarms with her cochlear implant off; it turns fire alarms and doorbells into light and vibration.
just_in.image_caption: Gargi Agrawalla holds the components of SIVO.GO, the AI alert device she designed as her final-year project at Loughborough University. The device won the UK James Dyson Award, carrying a £5,000 prize fund for its next stage of development.
just_in.nri_angle: An Indian-origin designer in the UK turned her own experience of deafness into an award-winning safety device — the kind of diaspora engineering story that starts in a dorm room and aims at every hotel room.

just_in.image_caption: YouTube / Barda Ni Bhomka
just_in.nri_angle: Dosanjh's stadium run links Wembley's diaspora crowd to a home-turf milestone, and his remarks speak to debates Punjabi audiences follow on both sides.

just_in.title: Deported in 1999, Brooklyn Man Can Still Seek Sale of Home Bought in 1985, Court Rules
just_in.excerpt: New York's Appellate Division held that because Clyde Nelson's 2007 divorce never disposed of the Brooklyn house, his ownership share survived — and his former wife cannot use the divorce to block his partition claim.
just_in.image_caption: The Brooklyn skyline in New York. A state appeals court ruled on November 18 that a co-owner removed from the US in 1999 can still seek the sale of a Brooklyn home bought in 1985.
just_in.nri_angle: The ruling shows removal from the US does not erase deed rights, and that a divorce silent on property leaves a deported spouse's share intact.

just_in.title: CAA Chief Bryan Lourd Urges Congress to Pass NO FAKES Act Against AI Deepfakes
just_in.excerpt: In a New York Times essay, the head of one of Hollywood's biggest talent agencies argues that the right to refuse an AI replica of your face or voice should be federal law — and that the stalled Senate bill can still pass this year.
just_in.image_caption: CAA chief executive Bryan Lourd, pictured in a Variety photograph.
just_in.nri_angle: A federal consent right over voice and likeness replicas would also protect ordinary families targeted by AI impersonation and scam calls.

just_in.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says He and Claude Have Proven the Riemann Hypothesis
just_in.excerpt: Levent Alpöge's proof exists as 17 million lines of computer-checked code rather than a paper, and the Clay Institute — which offers $1 million for the problem — still lists it as unsolved while review begins.
just_in.image_caption: A plot of the Riemann zeta function, whose non-trivial zeros the Riemann Hypothesis describes. Bernhard Riemann proposed the conjecture in 1859, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers  million for a correct proof.
just_in.nri_angle: A landmark AI research claim from the company many Indian-origin engineers and researchers work for, landing a day after its record Nasdaq debut.

immigration.title: Texas State Employee Faces Losing His Job as DACA Renewal Stalls
immigration.excerpt: Juan Rodriguez filed to renew his DACA work permit in April. It is still pending, and the permit that supports his state job expires in December.
immigration.nri_angle: Renewal delays that outrun USCIS's own 120-day goal are the practical risk for work-authorized immigrants, including Indian-origin DACA holders and their employers.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Princeton PhD Student Eva Yi Xie Detained by ICE After Neuroscience Conference
immigration.excerpt: Her lawyers say a pending asylum claim lets her stay; ICE says she never had authorisation to study in the US. A federal judge has barred her removal from Virginia while her habeas petition is heard.
immigration.image_caption: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement badge, in an Associated Press photograph. Princeton doctoral student Eva Yi Xie was detained by ICE at Reagan National Airport on November 19, 2026.
immigration.nri_angle: The detention happened on a domestic flight by a researcher with a pending asylum claim — a concrete reminder for international students and scholars in the US to verify their status with a lawyer before travelling, even inside the country.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Xie detained by ICE at Reagan National Airport
Judge Trenga bars removal from the Eastern District of Virginia
Government response to habeas petition due by 5 p.m.

immigration.title: NRI Seafarers Can Now Use a Job Contract or Seaman's Book to Open an NPS Account
immigration.excerpt: PFRDA's November 13 circular lets NRI seafarers use a valid employment contract or a Continuous Discharge Certificate with a disembarkation record under six months old as proof of address for NPS Tier I accounts.
immigration.nri_angle: Removes the overseas-address-proof barrier that kept NRI seafarers — a large Indian maritime workforce — out of NPS pension accounts.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: ICE Holds Texas Store Worker After Jail Term Over Customer's Private Photos
immigration.excerpt: Raghul Anandakrishnan, 29, was convicted of attempted invasive visual recording after a customer said he tried to AirDrop her intimate photos to himself. ICE took him from the Travis County jail and will hold him pending immigration court proceedings.
immigration.nri_angle: Shows how a local criminal conviction can move a non-citizen directly into ICE detention, and why sharing a phone passcode at a retail counter carries real risk.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: ICE Arrests Two on Sea-Tac Jetway, Delaying Los Angeles-Bound Flight
immigration.excerpt: Washington's governor called the jetway arrests 'deeply un-American' and urged airlines to push ICE out of airports; Alaska Airlines said it had no advance notice.
immigration.image_caption: A passenger is handcuffed by officers during an arrest at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday. ICE said the operation targeted a man who had overstayed his visa, and a second passenger was also arrested.
immigration.nri_angle: Airport arrests of visa overstayers are directly relevant to diaspora travelers with pending applications or past overstays flying US domestic routes.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Deported in 1999, Brooklyn Man Can Still Seek Sale of Home Bought in 1985, Court Rules
immigration.excerpt: New York's Appellate Division held that because Clyde Nelson's 2007 divorce never disposed of the Brooklyn house, his ownership share survived — and his former wife cannot use the divorce to block his partition claim.
immigration.image_caption: The Brooklyn skyline in New York. A state appeals court ruled on November 18 that a co-owner removed from the US in 1999 can still seek the sale of a Brooklyn home bought in 1985.
immigration.nri_angle: The ruling shows removal from the US does not erase deed rights, and that a divorce silent on property leaves a deported spouse's share intact.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Senate Bill Asks Labor Department for a Plan on PERM Premium Processing
immigration.excerpt: Appropriators want a report within 60 days of enactment on a fee-based fast track for green card labor certifications that now average about 300 days — but no premium option exists yet.
immigration.nri_angle: PERM is the first green card stage for most H-1B professionals, a heavily Indian cohort; a paid fast track would cut a roughly 300-day wait at the Labor Department stage.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Saudi Qualification Verification Disruptions Slow Work Visa Processing, Fragomen Warns
immigration.excerpt: The pre-entry degree-verification step for Saudi work visas is taking longer than usual, with some applications returned for resubmission and no official timeline for a fix — a delay that lands heavily on Indian recruits.

sources.label: Saudi Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

immigration.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian workforces in the Gulf; a stall at the verification stage delays joining dates and travel for Indian recruits across sectors.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: US Proposes PERM Overhaul: 90-Day Job Ads and Layoff Bars for EB-2, EB-3 Sponsors
immigration.excerpt: The Labor Department's first major PERM rewrite in two decades would lengthen recruitment, end the Schedule A bypass and bar sponsors with recent layoffs. It is a proposal only — comments close January 19, 2027, and current rules still apply.
immigration.nri_angle: PERM is the gateway step for most employer-sponsored green cards; Indian H-1B professionals in the EB-2/EB-3 backlog are the group most exposed to longer recruitment and the layoff bar.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Proposed rule published in the Federal Register (docket ETA-2026-0133)
Public comment period closes; DOL then decides on a final rule

immigration.title: H-1B Workers Are Giving Up on US Tech Jobs as Fees and Delays Pile Up
immigration.excerpt: Bloomberg profiles a Google engineer leaving for the UK on a Global Talent visa, and reports employers from IBM to Flywire rethinking US sponsorship as new charges and PERM suspensions stack up.
immigration.image_caption: Yash Sharma, a Google software engineer from India, photographed in San Francisco. Bloomberg profiled Sharma as he prepares to leave the United States for the United Kingdom after six years on an H-1B visa.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders are the largest group exposed to the new fees and PERM suspensions; the open PERM comment window through January 19, 2027 is the one dated action in the story.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Marriage to an Indian Citizen Gives No Right to Stay, Delhi High Court Rules
immigration.excerpt: Dismissing a US citizen's plea to convert her tourist visa into an X-1 spouse visa, Justice Amit Mahajan held that a foreigner's entry and stay are matters of sovereign discretion — and that a marriage certificate does not stop authorities from examining the circumstances.
immigration.image_caption: The emblem of the High Court of Delhi on the court gate in New Delhi, with media cameras gathered outside. The court held that marriage to an Indian citizen does not by itself confer a right to convert a visa into an Entry (X-1) visa or to stay in India.
immigration.nri_angle: Many diaspora families include a foreign-citizen spouse; the ruling confirms that marriage to an Indian citizen is grounds to apply for an X-1 visa, not a right to one.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: After Sikh Grandmother's Deportation, Bill Would Let Old Removal Orders Expire
immigration.excerpt: Four California Democrats introduced the Protect Our Neighbors Act on Thursday, citing Harjit Kaur, 73, who reported to ICE every six months for over 13 years before she was detained at a routine check-in and deported to India.
immigration.nri_angle: The bill responds to the deportation of a Sikh grandmother from California and would directly affect long-term Indian immigrants living in the US under old removal orders.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Adani Energy Wins 25-Year Bengal Deal for 1,750 MW of Round-the-Clock Renewable Power
markets-finance.excerpt: The Letter of Award from WBSEDCL covers 1,750 MW from July 2028, with a 750 MW option that would take the total to 2,500 MW if exercised. No tariff or contract value was disclosed.
markets-finance.image_caption: Archival photograph: Gautam Adani (right) at an event in West Bengal in September 2026. Adani Energy Solutions said its subsidiary has won a 25-year award to supply 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable power to the state discom.
markets-finance.nri_angle: For diaspora investors tracking Adani group stocks, the investable facts are the awarded 1,750 MW and 2028 start — the 2,500 MW headline includes an unexercised option, and no tariff was disclosed.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Wall Street's AI Selloff Deepens as S&P 500 and Dow Confirm Correction
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nasdaq fell 5.28% on Friday and erased its 2026 gains as Anthropic's debut fizzled and Nvidia slid 13.8%, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow more than 10% below their record closes.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Rupee Closes Above 93 for First Time in Seven Months, at 92.67 to the Dollar
markets-finance.excerpt: A fifth straight session of gains, powered by ₹84,290 crore of foreign equity inflows in nine November sessions and weaker crude, took the rupee past a level it last closed above on April 10.
markets-finance.image_caption: A graphic shows the US dollar and Indian rupee symbols side by side.
markets-finance.nri_angle: A rupee at 92.67 means each dollar remitted to India converts to fewer rupees than a week ago, while a sustained rally would ease India's import bill.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Who Is Anupama Ramachandran? The Chennai Cueist Who Became the First Indian Woman to Win a World Snooker Title — and Just Defended It at Home
sports.excerpt: Born in Chennai in 2002, Anupama Ramachandran chose snooker over chess at a Mylapore Club summer camp at 13, won a world under-16 title at 15, and in November 2025 became the first Indian woman to win the IBSF World Snooker Championship — then defended it in Indore on November 21, 2026, to become the first Indian to win back-to-back world snooker crowns, all while completing two postgraduate degrees.
sports.image_caption: Anupama Ramachandran lines up a shot at the snooker table during competition. The Chennai player won her first IBSF world title in Doha in November 2025 and defended the crown in Indore in November 2026.
sports.nri_angle: The Chennai cueist who became the first Indian woman to win a world snooker title — and the first Indian to defend one — gives diaspora fans a new name at the top of a sport India had never conquered, and a visible path for girls who want to follow her to the table.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Wins the IBSF World Snooker Championship in Doha, beating Ng On-yee 3–2 — the first Indian woman to win the title

sports.title: Pant's Wellington 128 Makes Him First Asian Keeper With Hundreds in All SENA Countries
sports.excerpt: Rishabh Pant's ninth Test century, reached with a six off Glenn Phillips, completed a set only two other wicketkeepers in history hold — and made him the sixth Indian batter with hundreds in South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
sports.nri_angle: A record Indian fans everywhere track: Pant now stands with Gilchrist and Bairstow as the only wicketkeepers with Test hundreds in all four SENA countries.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Post 720 for 9 at Wellington, Highest Test Total in New Zealand
sports.excerpt: Rahul's 136 and Pant's 128 headline an innings in which each of India's top five passed 80, leaving New Zealand 33 for 1 and fighting to avoid an innings defeat.
sports.nri_angle: A record Indian Test innings in Wellington gives diaspora fans a final day, starting Sunday US time, with India chasing an innings win.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Anupama Ramachandran Beats So Man Yan 3-1 to Defend World Snooker Title
sports.excerpt: The 3-1 win in Indore makes Anupama the first Indian to win back-to-back IBSF world snooker crowns, a year after her maiden title in Doha.
sports.image_caption: File photograph: Anupama Ramachandran lines up a shot during a snooker match.
sports.nri_angle: Anupama's back-to-back world titles give Indian cue sports a rare headline act for diaspora fans who follow Indian sport beyond cricket.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: KL Rahul's Wellington Hundred Completes SENA Sweep, a First for an Indian Opener
sports.excerpt: Rahul's 136 at the Basin Reserve was his first Test hundred in New Zealand, making him the first Indian opener — and the fifth Indian overall — with Test centuries in South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.
sports.nri_angle: A record Indian fans abroad can follow live in a two-match series in New Zealand, with the match state and the next day's play set out for readers in US and UK time zones.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India A Bowl Nepal Out for 26 in 306-Run Rising Stars Win in Doha
sports.excerpt: Centuries from Kumar Kushagra and Tilak Varma built 332 for 9 before Prince Yadav and Harshit Rana shared nine wickets in 11.3 overs, as Nepal posted the fifth-lowest total in List A history.
sports.image_caption: India A players celebrate during the Asia Cup Rising Stars match against Nepal in Doha.
sports.nri_angle: India A's emerging side is a window on the next generation of Indian cricket talent, and the Rising Stars tournament in Doha is a fixture diaspora fans track for future senior-team names.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Blind Cricket Team Boycotts Ceremony After Pakistan Awarded Washed-Out Asia Cup Final
sports.excerpt: The Dhaka final was abandoned without a ball bowled; a technical committee's joint-winners ruling was overturned in Pakistan's favour on net run rate, and India says it will not play Pakistan until the dispute is resolved.
sports.nri_angle: An India-Pakistan sporting dispute with a governance question at its centre, followed closely by cricket fans across the diaspora.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India A Face Pakistan Shaheens in Doha on Sunday in Rising Stars Asia Cup
sports.excerpt: Tilak Varma's India A meet the defending champions at West End Park at 3:30 p.m. IST on November 22, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi against teenage pacer Ali Raza the matchup to watch.
sports.nri_angle: The Doha fixture is watchable in the US and Canada on Willow TV and in India on Sony Sports and Sony LIV, with a 3:30 p.m. IST start on Sunday.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Jaiswal and Rahul's 130-Run Stand Blunts New Zealand's Advantage in Wellington
sports.excerpt: India reached 159 for 1 at stumps on Day 2 of the first Test, trailing New Zealand's 368 by 209 runs, after Yashasvi Jaiswal's 85 and KL Rahul's unbeaten 52 produced India's first century opening stand in 17 Tests.
sports.nri_angle: India's tour of New Zealand is a marquee series for the large Indian diaspora in New Zealand and for fans following from the US, the UK and the Gulf.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Proposes Common AI Limits Measured by Perplexity
technology.excerpt: Jakub Pachocki wants rival labs to agree a capability stop line — and not cross it until safety monitoring catches up. Altman called the essay the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI signage photographed at a company event. OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed that AI developers adopt common capability limits measured by perplexity, a proposal CEO Sam Altman endorsed publicly.
technology.nri_angle: A shared capability stop line would shape the models Indian-origin researchers and startups build on; for now it is a proposal with no threshold, date or signatories.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith Defends Overseas Data Centres After Trump's Penalty Threat
technology.excerpt: On Face the Nation, Smith split AI training sites from the cloud facilities that must sit near customers — while the Treasury secretary said he had not discussed Trump's proposal with him.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft President Brad Smith in a portrait photograph. Smith told CBS Face the Nation that cloud data centres serving overseas customers must be located near those customers, after President Trump threatened penalties on companies building data centres abroad.
technology.nri_angle: Microsoft's $17.5 billion India build-out in Chennai, Hyderabad and Pune sits inside the policy debate, but neither side named India as a target and no change was announced.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Cancer Vaccine Made for One Patient? Hyderabad's RNA Foundry Is Building It
technology.excerpt: PopVax's RNA Foundry aims to design personalised mRNA cancer vaccines from a patient's own tumour, at an estimated $300,000 and eight to ten weeks per vaccine — still experimental, and not yet given to any patient.
technology.nri_angle: A Hyderabad facility offering patient-specific cancer vaccines at a stated price is directly relevant to diaspora families who weigh treatment in India for relatives.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google's Willow Qubits Win a Game No Classical Strategy Can Match
technology.excerpt: Willow won the magic square game 98.3% of the time against an 88.9% classical ceiling, as Google Quantum AI measured quantum contextuality at scale in Science.
technology.nri_angle: A peer-reviewed hardware result from Google Quantum AI matters to India's large quantum research and tech workforce tracking where quantum advantage is actually coming from.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic Co-Founder to Make 'Large Gift' to Trump Accounts, Bessent Says
technology.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed the coming gift on CNBC a day after Anthropic's $93.5 billion IPO. Reuters identified the founder as Tom Brown; the amount has not been disclosed.
technology.image_caption: Anthropic executives and staff applaud at the Nasdaq podium on the company's listing day. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed a co-founder's planned gift to Trump Accounts a day after the IPO raised $93.5 billion.
technology.nri_angle: Trump Accounts are open to US-citizen children of immigrant families; the $1,000 Treasury seed for 2025–2028 births is money diaspora parents should claim.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Deaf Graduate's AI Alarm SIVO.GO Wins UK James Dyson Award and £5,000
technology.excerpt: Gargi Agrawalla, 23, built SIVO.GO from her own experience of missing alarms with her cochlear implant off; it turns fire alarms and doorbells into light and vibration.
technology.image_caption: Gargi Agrawalla holds the components of SIVO.GO, the AI alert device she designed as her final-year project at Loughborough University. The device won the UK James Dyson Award, carrying a £5,000 prize fund for its next stage of development.
technology.nri_angle: An Indian-origin designer in the UK turned her own experience of deafness into an award-winning safety device — the kind of diaspora engineering story that starts in a dorm room and aims at every hotel room.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google Gives IIT Kharagpur $5 Million to Accelerate AI Research and Training
technology.excerpt: The funding, announced during the institute's 75th anniversary, covers AI research in Indic languages, agriculture and materials science, plus training and campus capacity building.
technology.nri_angle: IIT Kharagpur's alumni network runs deep through US tech; Google's funding ties the institute's AI research in Indic languages and agriculture directly to that global talent pipeline.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: CAA Chief Bryan Lourd Urges Congress to Pass NO FAKES Act Against AI Deepfakes
technology.excerpt: In a New York Times essay, the head of one of Hollywood's biggest talent agencies argues that the right to refuse an AI replica of your face or voice should be federal law — and that the stalled Senate bill can still pass this year.
technology.image_caption: CAA chief executive Bryan Lourd, pictured in a Variety photograph.
technology.nri_angle: A federal consent right over voice and likeness replicas would also protect ordinary families targeted by AI impersonation and scam calls.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says He and Claude Have Proven the Riemann Hypothesis
technology.excerpt: Levent Alpöge's proof exists as 17 million lines of computer-checked code rather than a paper, and the Clay Institute — which offers $1 million for the problem — still lists it as unsolved while review begins.
technology.image_caption: A plot of the Riemann zeta function, whose non-trivial zeros the Riemann Hypothesis describes. Bernhard Riemann proposed the conjecture in 1859, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers  million for a correct proof.
technology.nri_angle: A landmark AI research claim from the company many Indian-origin engineers and researchers work for, landing a day after its record Nasdaq debut.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Scaler Cofounder Anshuman Singh Launches Arcfront, an AI Training Data Venture
technology.excerpt: Arcfront sells ‘Decision Arc Data’ — records of how experts reach decisions — to frontier AI labs; Singh says four of the five labs signed on within a year.
technology.nri_angle: Arcfront is hiring in Bengaluru as well as San Francisco, another example of Indian-founded teams selling data infrastructure to US frontier AI labs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Yash Patil, 23, Sells AI Startup Applied Compute to Palo Alto for $4.5 Billion
technology.excerpt: The Indian American co-founder, who left Stanford for OpenAI at 20, built Applied Compute from an idea in January 2025 to a $100 million revenue run-rate — and will become Palo Alto Networks' Co-Chief AI Officer when the all-stock deal closes.
technology.nri_angle: An Indian American founder's 18-month run from Stanford and OpenAI to a $4.5 billion acquisition by Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Idea for Applied Compute began taking shape.
Palo Alto Networks announced acquisition of Applied Compute.

technology.title: GlobalFoundries to Invest $10 Million in Cyient Semiconductors at $490 Million Valuation
technology.excerpt: The strategic stake in the Hyderabad chip-design company matches the price of its recent Edelweiss-led round and takes its combined post-money valuation to $510 million.
technology.nri_angle: A US foundry giant taking a stake in a Hyderabad chip designer underlines India's growing role in the global semiconductor design workforce, where much of the diaspora's tech community works.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ramayana Nears ₹1,700 Crore Worldwide, Passes Dhurandhar 2 in the US
entertainment.excerpt: Day 18 added ₹35.60 crore net in India as the worldwide gross hit ₹1,693.50 crore — and its $28.4 million US total is now the highest ever for an Indian film.
entertainment.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita in Ramayana. The film reached Rs 1,693.50 crore worldwide gross in 18 days and set a new all-time US record for an Indian film at $28.4 million.
entertainment.nri_angle: The film's $28.4 million US total is a new all-time benchmark for an Indian film in America, with overseas markets supplying a third of its global gross.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: A. R. Rahman Spent Three Years on 'Ramayana' Music, Turned Down 10–12 Films
entertainment.excerpt: At IFFI in Panaji, the composer said he set aside almost everything else for Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic, co-composing with Hans Zimmer — some pieces went through 12–13 versions.
entertainment.image_caption: A. R. Rahman with the Banaras team at a press conference during the International Film Festival of India in Goa.
entertainment.nri_angle: Rahman and Hans Zimmer's three-year score is the musical backbone of the Diwali epic diaspora audiences are watching in theatres now.
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ramayana: Part 1 Collects ₹64.10 Crore in Kerala in 17 Days
entertainment.excerpt: Trade tracker AB George's figures show the Nitesh Tiwari epic rebounding in its third Kerala weekend, while Pinkvilla puts its all-India nett at ₹850.50 crore and its dubbed versions past a ₹200 crore first.
entertainment.nri_angle: For diaspora audiences, the Kerala numbers underline how the film's dubbed versions — not just the Hindi original — are driving one of the biggest Indian theatrical runs of the year.

entertainment.nri_angle: Dosanjh's stadium run links Wembley's diaspora crowd to a home-turf milestone, and his remarks speak to debates Punjabi audiences follow on both sides.

food.nri_angle: A Jaipur home chef's garage-kitchen classes became a training pipeline through which nearly 200 women now earn from baking and cooking.

food.title: Krish Ashok Takes Food Myths From the Kitchen to the Body in 'Masala Body'
food.excerpt: The Masala Lab author's new book explains what the stomach, liver and intestines actually do, so readers can test the next frightening food forward themselves.

carousel.title: Princeton PhD Student Eva Yi Xie Detained by ICE After Neuroscience Conference
carousel.excerpt: Her lawyers say a pending asylum claim lets her stay; ICE says she never had authorisation to study in the US. A federal judge has barred her removal from Virginia while her habeas petition is heard.

carousel.nri_angle: The detention happened on a domestic flight by a researcher with a pending asylum claim — a concrete reminder for international students and scholars in the US to verify their status with a lawyer before travelling, even inside the country.

carousel.title: Who Is Anupama Ramachandran? The Chennai Cueist Who Became the First Indian Woman to Win a World Snooker Title — and Just Defended It at Home
carousel.excerpt: Born in Chennai in 2002, Anupama Ramachandran chose snooker over chess at a Mylapore Club summer camp at 13, won a world under-16 title at 15, and in November 2025 became the first Indian woman to win the IBSF World Snooker Championship — then defended it in Indore on November 21, 2026, to become the first Indian to win back-to-back world snooker crowns, all while completing two postgraduate degrees.
carousel.image_caption: Anupama Ramachandran lines up a shot at the snooker table during competition. The Chennai player won her first IBSF world title in Doha in November 2025 and defended the crown in Indore in November 2026.
carousel.nri_angle: The Chennai cueist who became the first Indian woman to win a world snooker title — and the first Indian to defend one — gives diaspora fans a new name at the top of a sport India had never conquered, and a visible path for girls who want to follow her to the table.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Proposes Common AI Limits Measured by Perplexity
carousel.excerpt: Jakub Pachocki wants rival labs to agree a capability stop line — and not cross it until safety monitoring catches up. Altman called the essay the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.
carousel.image_caption: OpenAI signage photographed at a company event. OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki has proposed that AI developers adopt common capability limits measured by perplexity, a proposal CEO Sam Altman endorsed publicly.
carousel.nri_angle: A shared capability stop line would shape the models Indian-origin researchers and startups build on; for now it is a proposal with no threshold, date or signatories.
